guide.title: Getting started
guide.description: All of GANIS in a few steps. Find it again anytime in Help › Getting started.

projects.title: Your projects
projects.text: The dashboard gathers your projects: novel, manga, film, series, game, tabletop RPG… Create one with “New project” (Ctrl+N); it opens right away.
points: Recently opened projects are at the top of the page.
Star a project to find it under “Favorites”.
Archive a finished project: it leaves the main list without being deleted.
The search bar filters projects by name or description.
A deleted project goes to the dashboard Trash: it can be restored there for 30 days, then it is permanently deleted.

spaces.title: Public space, private space
spaces.text: “Get started” opens the public space, without an account. Once signed in, you are in your private space. The two never mix.
points: Created without an account, a project is public: it is not encrypted, and anyone using GANIS on this computer can open, edit or delete it.
Created while signed in, a project is private: encrypted and only visible from your account.
To change it: project settings › Status and organization › Visibility.

Making a public project private requires signing in and typing its name again: it then disappears from the public space for everyone else. Making a private project public asks for confirmation: it is no longer encrypted.
Permanently deleting a public project (trash) requires typing its name again, because the other people on this computer lose it too.

layout.title: The workspace
layout.text: On the left, the module bar: Details, Characters, Locations, Structure, Plot, Notes and Search. The middle panel lists the module's features and items; each opens in a tab. Objects, Fauna and flora and Factions are added when you turn them on in the project settings.
points: Click a module again to collapse its panel.
Right-click a tab to pin it, or close the others, those on the left or on the right.
Pinned tabs come back the next time you open the project.
“Collapse” keeps only the icons in the left bar.
Each project type and module has its tutorial: the ? button at the top of the panel, or Help › Tutorial.

synopsis.title: The project home
synopsis.text: Every project starts with its sheet: synopsis, genres, tone and general information about the story.
points: Details › Project synopsis to write the summary.
Details › Glossary to define the words of your world and link them to sheets.
Name, description and type are edited in the project settings.
The status (preparing, in progress, paused, done) helps track progress.

characters.title: Characters
characters.text: Create your characters: identity, looks and personality, with three levels of detail as needed.
points: Characters › Create a character, or Ctrl+N in the module.
The level of detail of the sheets is set in the project settings.
Add a portrait and an image gallery to each sheet.
Each sheet opens in its own tab, named after the character.
Colour palette: its colours frame the character's portrait.

Below the sheet, three link sections: “Links with the world” (relationships, places, fauna and flora, items, factions, peoples, magic, grouped by type, with a single “Add a link” button), “Plot” and “Story”.
“Plot” and “Story” are hidden on sheets by default; show them in Project settings › Characters (or › Locations, › Items…). Only the display changes: the links are still used everywhere else.

locations.title: Locations
locations.text: From continent to room: each location has a sheet suited to its type (city, kingdom, forest…), and locations nest inside each other.
points: Locations › Create a location, then pick its type.
Place a location inside another to build your world's geography.
Add your own location types and statuses in the project settings.
Colour palette: as for characters, its colours frame the location's image.

world.title: Objects, fauna and flora, factions
world.text: Three optional modules: the objects in your story (weapons, vehicles, phones, magic items…), the animals and plants of your world, and factions (guilds, orders, clans, armies, cults…). They stay hidden until you turn them on.
points: Project settings › Objects (or Fauna and flora, or Factions): turn the module on, then keep only the categories you need.
An object can be stored in another (a key in a chest); a specific animal sits under its species.
A specific animal can also become a character: its character sheet is linked to it.
A faction can have branches (a section of an order, a family of a clan).
“Link an element” connects objects, species, factions, characters and locations: “owns”, “lives in”, “leads”, “is a member of”…

relations.title: Relationships and links
relations.text: Link your characters to each other (family, friendships, rivalries, alliances) and to their locations (home, origin…). The relationship graph shows your whole world at a glance.
points: Characters › Relationships to open the graph.
Character ↔ location links are managed from either sheet.
Structure items also show which characters and locations appear in them.

structure.title: Story structure
structure.text: Parts, chapters, scenes, or acts and sequences for a film: the outline adapts to the project type.
points: Structure › Story outline to build the tree.
Level names, numbering and colors are set in the project settings.
Each item has its own sheet, with its characters, locations and text.
“Move up” and “Move down” reorder the outline.

plot.title: The plot
plot.text: The plot board shows your storylines as columns, time flowing down, and their cause-and-effect links.
points: Add parallel storylines next to the main one.
Link two events: impact, influence or crossing.
Track each event's state: idea, draft, written, revised.
Plot › Read the story: the narrative in reading order.

notes.title: Notes and sticky notes
notes.text: Notes come with a real editor: headings, fonts, lists, tables, boxes, linked boxes and diagrams.
points: File your notes in folders.
The sticky-note wall holds loose ideas, placed freely.
Sheet descriptions also exist as system notes, editable from the notes, with font, size and lists.

search.title: Search
search.text: Find anything in the project: characters, locations, structure, documents, plot, notes and sticky notes.
points: The magnifier at the top right (or Ctrl+F) opens search in the middle panel: it looks through the whole project, ignoring accents and case.
Ctrl+K opens the palette: type to jump to an item or run a command.
Click a result to open it in a tab.

saving.title: Saving and versions
saving.text: A ● dot on a tab means unsaved changes. Save with Ctrl+S, or let autosave do it.
points: The status bar at the bottom always tells you where you stand: saving, saved or failed.
A version is created automatically at the start of each editing session.
“Versions” button: compare a previous state with the current one, then restore it if needed.
Name the current state to keep an important milestone.

trash.title: History, trash and undo
trash.text: A deletion can be undone right away with “Undo” (or Ctrl+Z). Deleted items stay 30 days in the trash.
points: Project › Trash to restore a deleted item.
Details › History: everything that happened in the project over the last 90 days.
In the history, click a name to open the item.

export.title: Back up and share
export.text: Export a project as a .ganix file to back it up or open it on another computer.
points: File › Export project (.ganix), or the download icon on the project card.
The .ganix file is not encrypted: keep it somewhere safe.
“Import a project” (with an account) adds it to your private space, or replaces an existing project after a backup.
Duplicate a project to try a variant without touching the original.

personalize.title: Your GANIS
personalize.text: Adapt the app to the way you work.
points: Light or dark theme in one click, in the top bar.
Packages: pick other color themes.
Settings: language, text size and account.
Work rhythm: your writing time day by day, and your streaks.

keyboard.title: Keyboard shortcuts
keyboard.text: Everything can be done from the keyboard too.
points: Ctrl+N create, Ctrl+S save, Ctrl+W close the tab.
Ctrl+Tab switch tabs, Ctrl+K find anything.
Alt or F10 moves the keyboard to the menu bar.
Full list: Help › Keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl+/).

shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts
shortcuts.description: GANIS shortcuts. Editor shortcuts work inside a note.

actions.togglePanel: Collapse or expand the middle panel (outside the editor)
actions.readStory: Read the whole story / exit reading

reference.undoDeletion: Undo the last deletion (outside a field)

about.tagline: The workshop for writers and screenwriters.
about.offline: GANIS works fully offline: your projects stay on this computer. Private projects are encrypted; public projects are not.
about.description: One place to build a story: characters, places, outline, plot, notes and documents, all linked, up to the readable version (▶ button).
about.dictionaries: Spelling dictionaries: French, Grammalecte (Olivier R., MPL 2.0); English, SCOWL (wordlist.sourceforge.net).

updates.title: Updates
updates.none: No version has been published yet.
updates.failed: Could not check: no connection, or the server is not responding. Try again later.
updates.openFailed: The download page could not be opened.
updates.auto: Check at startup (at most once a day)
updates.privacy: This is GANIS's only network connection: it only reads the latest version number from {{host}}. Nothing about your account or projects is sent, and nothing installs by itself.

whatsNew.title: What's new
whatsNew.description: What changed in GANIS, version by version.

v1_0_0.title: Clarity and safety
items: A small window explains the public space (shared on this computer, not encrypted) when you click “Get started”; the “Public space” badge reopens it.
Making a public project private, or permanently deleting a public project, requires typing its name again.
The status bar no longer shows “Saved” after a hidden failure: “Last save failed” until the next successful save.
Key names follow the interface language (Shift / Maj, Esc / Échap…).
Messages use real singular and plural forms.
Edit › Paste works from the menu.
New: Help › Report a problem, to copy useful technical information.
Save messages (success or failure) appear as notifications at the bottom of the screen: the page no longer moves.
Double-click: on a row of the outline, progress or history, and in the reading table of contents, it opens the sheet; on a plot lane header, it renames the lane.

report.title: Report a problem
report.description: GANIS works offline: nothing is sent automatically. Describe the problem, copy the information, then paste it into your message.
report.whatLabel: What were you doing when the problem happened? (optional)
report.whatPlaceholder: E.g. I moved a scene on the plot board, then the error message appeared.
report.privacy: No project content and no account name: only the version, system, display settings and latest error messages. Read the text before sending it.
report.howToSend: Paste this text into your message (email, form, ticket) to the person or service who supports you with GANIS. A screenshot helps too.
report.copied: Information copied: paste it into your message.
report.copyFailed: Copying failed: select the text above and copy it with Ctrl+C.

center.title: GANIS Help
center.description: How each part of the app works, and answers to common questions.

start.title: Getting started
start.intro: The dashboard gathers your projects: everything starts with “New project”.
items: “New project”: choose the kind of story (novel, manga / comic, film, series, video game, role-playing game or custom project). The kind decides the proposed structure (chapters, pages, scenes…) and the writing tools shown in the left bar.
Signed in to your account, a project is private and encrypted with your password. In the “Public space” (without an account), it is not encrypted: anyone using GANIS on this computer can open it.
The dashboard: search, recently opened projects, favourites (star), archived projects for those on hold, and the project trash, where a deleted project stays 30 days.
Help › Getting started guide tours the workspace in a few steps; Help › Tutorial walks you through your first moves; Help › Keyboard shortcuts lists them all.
This help opens on the section of the tab you are viewing. Its search finds a word in every section and in the frequently asked questions.
Help › What's new presents the changes in each version; Help › Report a problem… prepares a report to copy and send.

workspace.title: The workspace
workspace.intro: A project opens in the workspace: modules on the left, panel in the middle, tabs in the centre.
items: The left bar gives access to the modules: Details, Characters, Locations, Structure, Notes, and the project settings at the bottom. The magnifier at the top right (Ctrl+F) opens search.
The middle panel lists the module's features and items; a click opens a tab. Drag its right edge to widen it, or to the left to close it.
A single click in the middle panel opens a preview tab (italic title), replaced by the next one; a double-click, an edit or pinning keeps it. Can be changed in Settings › Appearance.
Tabs can be dragged. Right-click a tab to pin it, close the others, those to the right…
A ● dot on a tab means unsaved changes. The status bar at the bottom always shows whether everything is saved.
Ctrl+K opens the palette: type the name of a page, an action or an item to jump to it.

details.title: Project details
details.intro: The project home sums up your story; the synopsis tells it.
items: Project home: logo, description, type, status and synopsis preview.

Gallery: the project logo (shown on the home page, next to the name) and the images of the world and the story (posters, world maps, moods, sketches…), sorted into folders of up to 30 images. Drag and drop works; each image can be downloaded from its preview.
Synopsis: the story summary, with its genres, subgenres and tone.
Glossary: the words of your story (invented terms, places, concepts, titles…), in alphabetical order, with their definition, a category and links to sheets.
History: everything created, edited, deleted or restored in the project, day by day.
Trash: items deleted less than 30 days ago, ready to restore.

characters.title: Characters
characters.intro: Each character has a sheet, images and relationships.
items: The sheet has three detail levels (essential, intermediate, advanced), chosen for the whole project in the settings.
Main image and reference gallery: drop images straight onto the sheet.
Relationships: family, friends, rivals… The relationship graph shows everyone at a glance; characters can be moved freely.
Locations: where the character lives, works, grew up — optionally with the part of the story concerned.
Colour palette: its colours frame the character's portrait.
Powers: for stories where characters have powers, gifts or magic, turn on the “Powers” card in Project settings › Characters. It is added to every sheet, whatever the level of detail.

Family tree: in Relationships, “Tree” layout, choose a character to see their family only, generation by generation, from “Family” relations whose link is specified. A grandparent, uncle or cousin linked without the people in between makes those members appear as “Not mentioned” ghosts. Double-click a person to open their sheet.
Characters › List: every character as a grid or a table, with search, filters by role and status, and sorting.

Character relations: three views, Graph, Matrix and List. The graph offers several layouts (network, circle, by role, centred on one character, family tree); “Moment in the story” shows the relations at a given time.
Arcs: pick a character in the middle panel (the ↗ badge shows how many steps their arc has). Set the arc type, the belief at the start, the truth at the end, what they want and what they need.

Arcs, steps: each step is tied to a chapter or scene, with an inner state from −5 (trapped in their belief) to +5 (they have understood the truth), the character's choice and its consequence. The curve traces this change; clicking a point takes you to its step. Below, compare with the other characters' arcs.

locations.title: Locations
locations.intro: Locations nest: a continent contains kingdoms, which contain cities…
items: A location's type (city, forest, palace…) decides its sheet fields. You can create your own types in the settings.
The module panel shows locations as a tree; “Add a location in…” creates one inside another.
Each sheet has a banner, a gallery and the list of linked characters.
Colour palette: as for characters, its colours frame the location's image.

items.title: Objects
items.intro: The objects in your story: weapons, vehicles, clothing, phones, magic items…
items: Optional module: turn it on in Project settings › Objects, and it appears in the left bar. Turning it off deletes nothing.
Choose the categories you need (weapons, vehicles, magic…): only those are offered when creating. You can also add your own types.
The type chooses the sheet's fields: a weapon doesn't have the same information as a vehicle.
An object can be stored in another (a key in a chest, an engine in a ship): the panel shows them as a tree.
“Links with the world” connects the object to whoever owns, uses or seeks it, and to where it is, with a story period if needed (an object that changes hands).

species.title: Fauna and flora
species.intro: The animals and plants of your world, from a whole species to the individual with a name.
items: Optional module: turn it on in Project settings › Fauna and flora, and it appears in the left bar. Turning it off deletes nothing.
Choose fauna, flora or both. You can also add your own types.
An entry is either a whole species (grey wolves), or a specific animal or plant (Lightning, the hero's horse), placed under its species.
A specific animal can also be a character: “Create its character sheet” or link it to an existing character. The character sheet shows it in return.
“Links with the world” shows where it lives, what it eats, who it belongs to and what it is used for.

factions.title: Factions
factions.intro: The groups that drive your story: guilds, orders, clans, armies, cults, secret societies…
items: Optional module: turn it on in Project settings › Factions, and it appears in the left bar. Turning it off deletes nothing.
Choose the categories you need (political power, army, religion, crime…). The type chooses the fields: an army has its strength, a religion its dogmas and rites.
A faction can have branches: a section of an order, a cell of a network, a family of a clan.
Its leaders, founders, members and supporters are in “Links with the world”, with the characters. The exact role (captain, spy…) goes in the link's detail.
“Links with the world” also notes its allies, enemies, seat, the places where it is present and what it controls, with a story period if needed.

peoples.title: Peoples, cultures and religions
peoples.intro: The soul of your world: its peoples and races, their cultures, languages and beliefs.
items: Optional module: turn it on in Project settings › Peoples, cultures and religions, and it appears in the left bar. Turning it off deletes nothing.
Three categories: peoples and races, cultures and traditions (including languages), religions and beliefs (pantheons, deities, mythologies, prophecies). The type chooses the fields.
A sheet can contain others: a sub-people in its people, a branch in its religion, a deity in its pantheon.
“Links with the world” groups members, practitioners, speakers and worshippers, where a people lives and the powers it masters.
No duplicates with Factions: a religion (its beliefs, its rites) lives here, while the church or cult that organises it stays a faction, linked with “practises”.

magic.title: Magic and powers
magic.intro: The shared rules of power in your world: where it comes from, what it costs, its limits, its schools and techniques.
items: Optional module: turn it on in Project settings › Magic and powers, and it appears in the left bar. Turning it off deletes nothing.
Three levels: the system (magic, inner energy, superpowers, divine power, psionics, alchemy), its schools and branches (elements, bloodlines), then its spells and techniques.
The type chooses the fields: a system has its source, rules, cost and limits; a technique its effects, power, range and risks.
“Links with the world” groups those who master it and those who teach it, its sources and who forbids it.
No duplicates: a character's own powers stay on their “Powers” card; link them to the system with “masters”.

structure.title: Story structure
structure.intro: Your story's outline, adapted to the project type.
items: Novel: parts, chapters, scenes. Film: acts, sequences, scenes. Manga: volumes, chapters, pages… Names can be changed in the project settings.
Numbers are computed for you; an item can be left out of the numbering (prologue, interlude).

A structure item sheet gathers all its links in “Links with the world”, sorted by kind: characters (point of view, present…), places, and world entries (an item at the heart of the scene, a faction present, a magic mentioned). “Add a link”, in the card title, asks for the kind, then the item and its role; the pencil on a row changes the role or removes the link. A world entry can also be linked to an item from its “Story” section.
Automatic numbering (renumbering on every move) is turned on in the project settings, as is each level's colour.

Documents: in an item's sheet, keep its files (manga pages, PDFs, Word files, images, sounds…) with “Add files” or by drag and drop. They are stored in the project (encrypted if the project is private) and exported in the .ganix.

Click a document to read it in GANIS; “Read the pages” chains a chapter's images. “Edit in its application” opens it in Word, Acrobat, Clip Studio…: every save comes back, the previous content stays in the versions.
Structure › Continuity: each character's path item by item (role, state, changes) and the presence table. Link characters in a scene's sheet, then note their state in its “Continuity” card.

manuscript.title: Novel
manuscript.intro: The Novel module gathers the book's text and the tools to write it, track its progress and present it.
items: The text is written in each scene's sheet (“Text” card), or comes from a Word or text document kept on the scene. The scene's “Writing” card holds its word goal, drafting state, point of view and narration (person, tense).
Novel › Manuscript: the whole book in one piece, in outline order, with contents, word count and reading time. It exports to Word, PDF or text.

Novel › Progress: words per chapter, the novel's goal and words left, drafting states, point of view. Scenes whose narration differs from the rest of the novel (another person, another tense) are flagged.
“Today” tracks your daily word goal, the current session (“New session” starts again from zero), your streak and the last 30 days. The status bar shows the words written today.

Novel › Replace fixes a name or a word in the text of every scene (case, whole word). Tick the occurrences to replace: a version of each changed scene is kept, and “Undo” reverses the whole replacement.

Novel › Import takes a Word (.docx), Markdown (.md) or text (.txt) file and splits it into parts, chapters and scenes (* * * separators cut scenes). You check the proposed structure before importing, and the import can be undone in one click.

Novel › Editorial file: a one-line pitch, a short summary and a long summary, to present the novel to a publisher or agent. “From the synopsis” starts from the project synopsis; each text exports on its own and keeps its versions.
Novel › Continuity: a character's path scene by scene (role, state, changes) and the presence table by chapter. The state is noted in each scene's “Continuity” card.

script.title: Manga / comic
script.intro: The Script module follows a manga or comic page by page, from writing to production.
items: Script › Flatplan shows a volume's pages as spreads, in the chosen reading direction. A page shows the art filed on its sheet; otherwise, art filed on the chapter is shared out in order. The first printed page decides which pages face each other: a reveal planned at the page turn on an even page is flagged.

Non-story pages (cover, title page, contents, credits, bonus, afterword…) are added below the flatplan. They take their place in the spreads and the page numbers; covers stand apart, without a page number.

Script › Production tracking gives each page its step (storyboard, pencils, inks, screentones, lettering, approved), one page or a whole selection at a time. The flatplan can show these steps in colour (“Show: Production”).
“Export the script”, in the flatplan, saves the volume script for the artist (Word, PDF or text): characters and locations first, non-story pages, each page's number, panels and texts.

A chapter's sheet creates its pages in one go (“Add pages”). File each piece of art on its page's sheet: it shows next to the panels, and the chapter's “Read the pages” chains them. Panels are found by the search and kept in the page's versions.
Script › Reading: the story chapter by chapter, with each chapter's explanation (its summary), then what its pages show.
Script › Progress: planned and written pages, statuses and amount of text.
Script › Continuity: where each character appears, and in what state, panel by panel.

screen.title: Film and series
screen.intro: The Screenplay module of a film or series writes in the standard format and prepares the shoot.
items: Film: each scene sheet has its script in standard format (INT. / EXT. heading, location, time; actions, lines, transitions, shots, notes). A sequence sheet tracks its writing status and estimated runtime (one script page per minute).

Film: Screenplay › Film tracking gathers the film sheet (logline, target runtime, writer), the estimated runtime of the whole film against the target, the runtime and share of each act, the status of the sequences and the lines per character.

Film: Screenplay › Script reading shows the whole film, scenes numbered, and exports it to Word, PDF, text or Fountain: a title page (writer, logline), without act or sequence titles, like a feature screenplay.

Film: the film sheet (Screenplay › Film tracking) holds the logline, pitch and statement of intent; “Export the dossier” adds the project synopsis, characters, step outline and treatment, built from the plan, as Word, PDF or text.

Film: Screenplay › Breakdown gives, for each scene, the characters and their state, the linked sheets, and the extras, props, wardrobe, effects… to plan; the Shooting schedule tab groups scenes by set, interior or exterior, day or night.
Film: Screenplay › Index cards shows one card per scene, in its act's colour; drag a card to move it, even into another sequence.

Film: in script reading, “Revisions” locks scene numbers (an added scene becomes 12A) and starts a coloured revision: anything changed afterwards is marked with an asterisk. Choosing an actor keeps only their scenes, for auditions. The PDF export follows the standard format (Courier 12, 55 lines per page, (MORE) and (CONT'D)).

Film: Screenplay › Import a screenplay brings in a Fountain or Final Draft (.fdx) file; characters and locations are linked to sheets with the same name, or created. In a scene sheet, suggestions follow your typing (transitions, shots, character and location names).

Series: Screenplay has the same tools as the film — Index cards (one column per episode), Breakdown and shooting schedule across episodes, Fountain or Final Draft import, revisions and locked numbers (episode.scene: 2.5, then 2.5A). Episode tracking shows each episode's due date (in red once passed), speaking time by episode, and “Export the bible” assembles the concept, characters, seasons and their episodes.

Film: Film tracking places the structure beats (inciting incident, plot points, midpoint, climax) on scenes and tells you whether they fall too early or too late; each character's speaking time shows by act, with their longest absence.

reading.title: Full reading (▶)
reading.intro: The ▶ button, on the right of the title bar, “runs” the project: the whole story is compiled in outline order and shown on its own, full screen.
items: Novel: the continuous manuscript, chapter after chapter.

Manga / comic: the story chapter by chapter, like a novel: what each chapter is about (its summary), then what its pages show, one after the other. Panel details (framing, balloons, sound effects…) stay in the page sheets.
Film: the script in standard format, scene by scene, numbered across the whole film.
Series, video game, role-playing game, custom project: each outline item with its summary, its text or documents, or failing that the plot events attached to it.
F5 does the same. Press again (or the ■ button) to return to the editing layout.
The reading updates itself: moving a scene in the outline moves it in the reading. It exports to Word, PDF or text.

plot.title: Plot
plot.intro: The board of parallel plots: one column per plot, time going down.
items: Double-click a column to place an event; drag cards to change their moment or plot.
Drag a card's round handle onto another to create a link: impact, influence or crossing.
Link each event to the project: point of view, characters present, location, structure chapter and notes.
“Story reading” shows the events in reading order (by default the structure's) with everything attached, chapter documents included.
Character, location, structure item and world sheets (items, factions…) show their events in their “Plot” section. In an event’s panel, “Items, fauna and flora, factions…” adds world entries to it.
Ctrl+Z undoes each action on the board. The “Tension” button shows the tension curve; plot colours are set in Project settings › Plot.

Timeline: the plot events placed by their date in the story, one row per plot line, with the eras in the background. It opens year by year at the start of the story; the “Story starts” button takes you back there.
Zoom: the − / + buttons or + / − keys (one mark gap at a time), or Ctrl + wheel. To move: drag the timeline, use the horizontal wheel (or Shift + wheel), or the overview below the plot lines.
Click an event on the timeline to see its details and the characters’ ages; ← → move from one event to the next in time. The “Key” button explains the shapes.

In the timeline toolbar, “Event” and “Eras” open the right panel: the details of the chosen event, or your world’s eras, to create and edit (clicking an era band opens it too). The date precision and the name of the years are set in the project settings › Plot.
“Walk through” follows the story event by event on the board: in outline order, in reading order, or a single plot line from start to end, with what each event triggers.
Mysteries: a question the reader wants answered. Plant its clues in events, choose the event of the reveal and track its status (open, solved, dropped).
Structure templates: three acts, hero's journey… place the acts and the main beats on the board's moments; you can also create your own.
Automatic pointers: invitations to look at the structure (isolated plot line, untitled event, link going back in time…), never automatic fixes.

“Events from the structure” creates an event for each item of an outline level (each chapter, for instance), tied to that item and with its summary. The clean view hides the bars to focus on the board.

notes.title: Notes and sticky notes
notes.intro: Everything that doesn't fit elsewhere: research, ideas, documentation.
items: The editor offers headings, fonts, sizes, colours, lists, tables and links. Less common tools are in the “…” menu at the end of the bar.
Sticky-note box: a coloured block in the text. Linked boxes: steps joined by arrows, with “+” to insert more. Diagram: boxes you move and connect with the mouse.

Mention a project item, in a note or in a novel scene's text: “$$” followed by a few letters searches the whole project. A letter between two “$” shows one kind only: “$c$” characters, “$l$” locations, “$s$” structure, “$w$” world (items, wildlife, factions, peoples, magic), “$n$” notes, “$i$” gallery images. French letters work too: “$p$” characters, “$d$” structure, “$u$” world. Clicking the link opens the sheet.
File notes in folders by dragging them in the panel; pin the most important ones.
The sticky-note wall holds loose ideas: move them by their strip, resize them by their corner.
Inspiration board: gallery images, colours, quotes and notes, laid out freely to set the story's mood.

search.title: Search
items: The magnifier at the top right, or Ctrl+F, opens search in the middle panel. It looks through the whole project: characters, locations, world sheets, structure, documents, plot, notes (including their content) and sticky notes.
Accents and capitals don't matter: “chateau” finds “Château”. Several words: all must appear.
Ctrl+K opens the palette, which also offers pages and actions.

history.title: History, versions and trash
items: After a deletion, “Undo” appears for a few seconds (or Ctrl+Z outside a field). After that, the item stays 30 days in the trash.
Restoring an item also brings back everything that went with it: images, relationships, sub-items…

Versions: the “Versions” button of a note, the synopsis or a sheet shows its earlier states, compares them with the current one (removed in red, added in green) and lets you go back. The current state is kept before any restore.
A version is taken automatically at the start of each editing session; you can also create a named one (“Before rewrite”).
The project history (Details › History) lists every action of the last 90 days.

files.title: Projects, files and security
files.intro: Your projects stay on this computer.
items: Each private project is encrypted: without your password, its data can't be read. Public projects (created without an account) are not encrypted and can be opened by anyone who uses GANIS on this computer.
Export as .ganix (File › Export) makes a full copy of the project, to keep as a backup or open on another computer. Note: this file is not encrypted.
Import a .ganix (File › Import) adds the project, or replaces the existing one (the previous version first goes to the project trash, encrypted, for 30 days).
GANIS works fully offline.

settings.title: Settings
items: Project settings (bottom of the left bar): information, statuses, character detail level, location types, structure and colours, and Plot (plot line colours, the timeline's date precision and the name of the years).
Objects, Fauna and flora, Factions, Peoples, Magic: turn these optional modules on and choose their categories.
General settings (gear at the top): account, password, recovery key, language, theme, autosave.
Packages: colour themes for the whole app.

about.title: About GANIS
about.intro: GANIS is the workshop for authors and screenwriters: one place to build a story, from the first idea to a readable version.
items: For every kind of story: novel, manga / comic, film, series, video game, role-playing game, or a custom project with your own outline.
Characters, places, relations, outline, plot, notes and documents stay linked: what changes in one place shows everywhere.

Offline: GANIS relies on no online service. Your projects stay on this computer (private projects encrypted with your account, public projects unencrypted); a project travels elsewhere as a .ganix file.
Spell checking: Hunspell dictionaries for French (Grammalecte, MPL 2.0 licence) and English (SCOWL, wordlist.sourceforge.net).
Version, information and credits: Help menu › About GANIS.

items.q: I deleted something by mistake.
items.a: Click “Undo” in the message that appears, or press Ctrl+Z. Later: Project › Trash, then “Restore”.

items.q: I edited a sheet and want to go back.
items.a: Open the sheet, click “Versions”, pick the state you want and click “Restore this version”.

items.q: How do I keep my manga chapter in GANIS?
items.a: Open the chapter's sheet (story outline › click the chapter), then “Add files” or drop all the pages on the “Documents” card. Put them in order (Alt+↑/↓), then “Read the pages” for continuous reading.

items.q: I edited a document in Word: is it up to date in GANIS?
items.a: Yes, if it was opened with “Edit in its application”: every save in Word comes back within seconds. Click “Finish” when you are done (the unencrypted working copy is then deleted).

items.q: How do I read my story in the order the reader discovers it?
items.a: Link the plot events to chapters (“Told in” field), then open Plot › Story reading: the order follows the structure. You can also choose a manual order at the top of the reading view.

items.q: Are my changes saved?
items.a: Look at the status bar, bottom right: “Saved at …” means everything is saved. Ctrl+S saves the tab; “Save all” saves everything.

items.q: I forgot my password.
items.a: On the sign-in screen, choose “Forgot password” and enter your recovery key (6 groups of 6 characters), given when the account was created.

items.q: How do I work on another computer?
items.a: Export the project as .ganix (File › Export), copy the file, then import it in GANIS on the other computer.

items.q: Why don't chapter numbers change when I move them?
items.a: Automatic numbering is off by default. Turn it on in Project settings › Structure, or renumber by hand.

items.q: How do I rename “Part, Chapter, Scene”?
items.a: Project settings › Structure › Customise: each level's name, numbering and colour.

items.q: An image won't add.
items.a: GANIS accepts PNG, JPEG, WebP and GIF, up to the size shown. Save the image again as JPEG or make it smaller.

items.q: I deleted a project by mistake.
items.a: Click “Undo” in the message that appears, or open Trash on the dashboard and choose “Restore”. A project stays in the trash for 30 days before being permanently deleted.

items.q: How do I lock GANIS when I step away?
items.a: Settings › Account › Automatic lock: choose a delay. After that time without activity, your password is required to resume; your tabs stay open.

items.q: I can't find objects, fauna and flora or factions.
items.a: These modules are hidden by default. Open Project settings › Objects (or Fauna and flora, or Factions) and turn them on: they appear in the left bar, under Locations.

items.q: My animal talks and has relationships: character or animal?
items.a: Both. Create it in Fauna and flora as “a specific animal or plant”, then click “Create its character sheet”. The two entries are linked.

items.q: How do I frame an entry's image with colours?
items.a: Add colours in the entry's “Colour palette” field (character, location, object, fauna and flora): a frame of those colours surrounds its image.

items.q: How do I follow a character's change through the story?
items.a: Characters › Arcs: pick the character in the middle panel, note what they believe at the start and understand at the end, then add a step for each key moment, tied to its chapter, with their inner state. The curve draws itself.

items.q: How do I change a name throughout my novel?
items.a: Novel › Replace: type the old and the new name, check the ticked occurrences, then “Replace”. A version of each changed scene is kept, and “Undo” reverses everything.

items.q: How do I bring my Word manuscript into GANIS?
items.a: Novel › Import: choose the file (.docx, .md or .txt), check the proposed split into parts, chapters and scenes, then “Import”. “Undo the import” takes you back.

items.q: How do I place my events in the story's time?
items.a: Give each event a year (in its details, on the board or on the timeline), then open Plot › Timeline. To go down to the month, day or hour, set the precision in the project settings › Plot.

items.q: Where do I create the great periods of my world?
items.a: On the timeline, “Eras” button: “Add an era”, then its name, years and colour. It shows as a band above the years.

items.q: How do I track a mystery's clues?
items.a: On the plot board, create a mystery (its question), plant its clues in events and choose the event where the answer is revealed.
